extractionNotes: EXTRACTION COMPLETE: all three Years (SHS 1/2/3) across all three Strands and all eight Sub-Strands have now been read and captured from the main curriculum body (printed pages 25-146, PDF pages 27-148). Final body-content totals are 24 Sub-Strand-year blocks (8 Sub-Strands x 3 Years), 24 Content Standards, 24 Learning Outcomes, and 65 Learning Indicators. This falls short of the document's own Scope-and-Sequence summary table total of 70 Learning Indicators by 5; per the pre-existing note below (and re-confirmed during this pass), that summary table extracts as severely garbled/misaligned and is NOT used as ground truth -- the body content, read directly strand-by-strand and sub-strand-by-sub-strand, IS the ground truth. The shortfall is concentrated in Year Three's Strand 3 (Analysis and Interpretation): both of its Sub-Strands (3.3.1 Critically Responding..., 3.3.2 Connecting Artworks...) contain only ONE Learning Indicator each in the raw text, versus 2-3 LIs each for the equivalent Year One/Year Two sub-strands; confirmed by direct text search (no '3.3.1.LI.2', '3.3.2.LI.2', etc. codes appear anywhere in the extracted text). This is recorded as a genuine source-document/extraction-limitation finding, not corrected by fabricating additional Learning Indicators to reach 70.

TWO APPENDICES FOUND (printed pages 147-175, PDF pages 149-177-- i.e. extending a few pages beyond the stated 175-page count, likely because the count in the task brief was approximate): APPENDIX I is titled (per partially legible glyphs) a 'Prescribed Repertoire List for Music & Dance Performing Arts Skills', attached to Sub-Strand 2 (Skills in Performance); the overwhelming majority of its content (a multi-column repertoire/resource table) extracts as unreadable corrupted glyph sequences (e.g. 'sZZ Wt^ W^', 'ZZZZZZZZZZZ') under pdftotext -layout, almost certainly due to a custom/embedded font in the source PDF whose character-to-glyph (cmap) mapping pdftotext cannot resolve -- this is a PDF-authoring defect, not fixable by re-running extraction with different flags. A handful of fragments ARE legible within the garbled table, preserved here for reference only (not attributed to any curriculum node, since they cannot be reliably placed in context): repertoire titles '1. Where'er you walk (G.F. Handel)', 'Tuu Tuu Gbvi (F Major)', 'Enkyr (G Major)', 'Yang Yang K'ole'; a citation 'Mereku, C.W.K. (1984) Six Atntbn Pieces Compiled by Eva Ebeli (2002). Winneba: UEW Music Department.'; and a URL 'www.3wstore.com/amazon_store/item/0970443900'. No Category A (Strand/Sub-Strand/CS/LO/LI/Assessment) content is present in Appendix I -- it is purely a supplementary resource/repertoire list, analogous to a Teaching-and-Learning-Resources appendix, so (per the canonical schema's treatment of front matter/appendices as document-level context rather than per-node fields) it is not modelled in the strands[] tree. APPENDIX II is a 'GLOSSARY OF PERFORMING ARTS TERMS', in three visibly distinct parts: (a) an initial combined 'DANCE AND DRAMA TERMS' + 'MUSIC TERMS' section (printed pages 152-159 approx.) that IS fully legible -- a genuine, well-formed glossary of dozens of terms (e.g. 'acting', 'choreography', 'atntbn', 'cadence', 'solfege', etc.); (b) a second, separate 'DANCE' and then 'DRAMA' section immediately following (printed pages 160-164 approx.) that is severely garbled in the same way as Appendix I (term names and most definition text unreadable, e.g. 'ZZZZZZZZZZZ'), again apparently due to embedded-font corruption; and (c) a final glossary section of VISUAL ARTS terminology (terms like 'printmaking', 'primary colours', 'relief', 'warp', 'weft', 'silhouette') that is fully legible but is FLAGGED NEEDS_REVIEW as likely out-of-scope content -- a Visual Arts glossary has no obvious place in a Dance/Music/Drama 'Performing Arts' curriculum document, and this document already has one confirmed copy-paste leak from a different subject (the Agricultural Science TOC entries documented below), so this may be a second such leak rather than a deliberate cross-reference. None of Appendix II's content maps onto the Strand/Sub-Strand/Content-Standard/Learning-Outcome/Learning-Indicator/Assessment schema (it is reference/glossary material), so -- consistent with how this schema treats front matter -- it is documented here at the document level rather than forced into the strands[] tree or fabricated where illegible.

Page-number offset confirmed: printed footer page number = raw PDF page index minus 2 throughout the sampled range (e.g. PDF page 27 prints footer 'PERFOEMING ARTS | 25'; PDF page 50 prints footer '48 | PERFOEMING ARTS'). Used to derive 'page' from 'pdfPageIndex' and vice versa for all source objects below; individual node page numbers are best-effort (content for a single node frequently spans a page break) rather than pixel-exact.

The Scope and Sequence summary table (PDF page 25, printed page 23) extracts severely garbled/misaligned via pdftotext -layout -- rows, sub-strand names, and per-year CS/LO/LI count columns are jumbled together (e.g. 'Performing Arts Literature' appears as a sub-strand name in the garbled table but does not match any of the actual 4 Strand-1 sub-strand headings encountered in the body: RUDIMENTS IN PERFORMING ARTS, SKILLS IN PERFORMANCE, COMMUNICATIONS IN THE PERFORMING ARTS, BUSINESS CYCLE IN THE PERFORMING ARTS). The table's own printed overall totals line is legible and unambiguous, however: 'Content Standards 24 / Learning Outcomes 24 / Learning Indicators 70' -- matching the prior inventory pass exactly. The per-sub-strand/per-year breakdown numbers in this table are NOT used as ground truth in this extraction (body content, read directly, is the ground truth instead); flagged NEEDS_REVIEW at the document level rather than transcribing the garbled table.

Curriculum code formatting is inconsistent across sub-strands within the same document, preserved verbatim rather than normalised: Strand 1 Sub-Strand 1 (Rudiments in Performing Arts, Year One) prints its Learning Outcome code as '1.1.1.LO1' (no dot before the final digit) and its Content Standard code as '1.1.1CS1' (no dots at all between the numeric prefix and 'CS1'). All other Year-One sub-strands print Learning Outcome and Content Standard codes with full dot-separation (e.g. '1.1.2.LO.1', '1.1.2.CS.1', '1.1.3.LO.1', '1.1.3.CS.1', '1.1.4.LO.1'), EXCEPT Strand 1 Sub-Strand 4 (Business Cycle in the Performing Arts) whose Content Standard is dotted ('1.1.4.CS.1') but whose Learning Indicator codes are printed WITHOUT a dot before 'LI' ('1.1.4LI.1', '1.1.4LI.2', '1.1.4LI.3', '1.1.4LI.4') while the paired Assessment codes ARE dotted ('1.1.4.AS.1' etc). All codes preserved exactly as printed in the 'code' fields below.

This curriculum genuinely integrates three art forms (Dance, Music, Drama) under single Learning Outcomes/Content Standards, confirmed throughout Year One: a single Learning Outcome (e.g. 1.1.1.LO1) is followed by three separate Learning Indicators, one per art form (1.1.1.LI.1 = Dance, 1.1.1.LI.2 = Music, 1.1.1.LI.3 = Drama), each phrased near-identically except for the substituted art-form name and its discipline-specific vocabulary. This pattern (one LI per art form under a shared LO/CS) recurs for 1.1.2 (6 LIs = roughly 3 art forms x repertoire-stage) but NOT for every sub-strand (1.1.3 has only 2 LIs, 1.1.4 has 4 LIs organised by business-process stage rather than by art form) -- preserved exactly as printed per sub-strand, not forced into a uniform pattern.

The GESI/SEL/National-Core-Values cell in this document's Learning-Outcome rows is structured differently from the Physics/Robotics/Biomedical-Science template: after the initial 'GESI: ...' paragraph (with its own bullet list), the SAME cell continues with three further named sub-headers -- 'Leadership and Respect for Others' Views:', 'Diversity:', 'Equity:' -- before the 'SEL: ...' block and the final 'National Core Values: <comma-separated list>' line followed by a one-line definition of each named value. Because the canonical schema's guidance object has no dedicated slot for the 'Leadership and Respect for Others' Views / Diversity / Equity' sub-headers or for the per-value definition sentences, this extraction folds the GESI paragraph together with those three sub-headers verbatim into guidance.gesi (as a single string, in source reading order), and stores the National Core Values definitions verbatim in an added guidance.nationalCoreValuesDescriptions array (one string per value, 'Name: definition text'), alongside the plain guidance.nationalCoreValues name array required by the canonical schema. This is a documented subject-specific extension per the schema's own design note ('add a subject-specific optional field rather than distorting the shared shape'), not a fabrication.

No Learning Outcome row sampled so far in Year One carries its own standalone Pedagogical-Exemplar-style bullet distinctly separated from the Learning-Indicator cell; Pedagogical Exemplars are attached at the Learning Indicator level only, consistent with the canonical schema.

Teaching and Learning Resources grids print as multi-column layouts that wrap unpredictably under pdftotext -layout (column headers/items visually bleed across cells at page breaks, e.g. Sub-Strand 2's TLR table mixes generic items 'Writing Pads/Pens/Projector/Flip Chart/Video Camera' with per-art-form lists 'Musical TLR:', 'Drama TLR:' and short physical/kinaesthetic terms 'Time/Space/Force/Body' in what appears to be a 4-column grid). learningOutcomes.description: Apply the elements of the Performing Arts to develop, compose, and perform artistic product(s) in [DANCE, MUSIC, and DRAMA, or a collaboration]).

guidance.twentyFirstCenturySkills: Communication & Collaboration: Learners learn by communicating and collaborating: by working together to develop an understanding and application of elements in Dance, viz., body, space, force, and time; by working together to develop an understanding and application of rudiments in Music, viz., scale, note durational values, time beat patterns, tempo, dynamics, and simple forms; by working together to develop an understanding and application of elements in Drama, viz., synopsis, character, acting, props, choreography, sound effects, scenery, properties, lighting, costume, and make-up; through display of artistic non-verbal communication such as facial expressions, cues, gestures etc.; by varying the levels of details and the language used during performance to make it appropriate to the audience; by working together to develop, compose, rehearse and perform own creative works. Critical Thinking & Problem Solving: Learners solve problems through critical thinking, by demonstrating a thorough understanding of a generalised concept and facts specific to emerging issues. Leadership and Personal Development: Learners acquire leadership and psycho-social skills through the various roles taken in the design, composition and performance processes. Cultural Identity and Global Citizenship: By composing songs, dances and other artistic products based on cultural and national issues of interest.
guidance.gesi: GESI: Learners having experienced a teaching approach that ensures gender equality and social inclusion, where they work with each other in an inclusive way; cross-sharing knowledge and understanding among groups and individuals lead them to: respect individuals' creativity, imagination, experiences, and cultures, in the Performing Arts; awareness creation on the spirit of teamwork in producing artworks to avoid artistic egos; interrogate and dispel misconceptions/myths, stereotypes and biases about gender and the role men and women play in the Performing Arts; identify injustice, especially in recognition of the contributions of different groups and individuals to the effective creation of artworks. Leadership and Respect for Others' Views: Inculcate the habit of leadership through teamwork; respect for individuals' views, beliefs, religions, and cultures. Diversity: Promote divergent views to ensure inclusivity in the learning of the Performing Arts. Equity: Develop fair and impartial opportunities or resources for learners devoid of unwanted segregation or discrimination among Performing Art learners.

The teacher takes Learners through the following activities: a. Explore how the emerging global issues and historic belief systems affect creative choices in DANCE/MUSIC/DRAMA work; b. Discuss how the artistic product(s) communicates new perspectives or realizations. Compare orally and in writing the process used in choreography/composition/playwrighting to that of other creative, academic, or scientific procedures; c. Identify how compositions are appropriate for an audience or context, and how this will shape future compositions; d. Analyse aurally the elements of music (including form) of musical works, relating them to style, mood, and context, and describe how the analysis provides models for personal growth as composer, performer, and/or listener.
Exploratory Learning: Design concept maps to link the artworks to everyday life experiences.

Talk for Learning (TfL): Through a teacher-led discussion, brainstorm the connection between various life experiences and various ideas in a performing art creative product(s). Teacher encourages Learners to watch the Post-Production recording and respond to the video documentary played in class or taken home and describe the activities involved (culturally, historically, musically, dramatically, artistically, etc.) and connect with their personal interests, experiences, ideas, and knowledge.

Project-Based Learning: Individually, write down how your life experiences, ideas and perspectives are realised through a performing art artistic product(s) you have watched connected to everyday life.

Talk-for-Learning: Through a teacher-led discussion, brainstorm on the connection between various life experiences and various ideas in the artistic product(s); Teacher encourages Learners to describe various life experiences and activities involved (culturally, historically, musically, dramatically, artistically, etc.) and connect with their personal interests, experiences, ideas, and knowledge; Learners demonstrate a correlation between DANCE, MUSIC, and DRAMA, and possibly, VISUAL ARTS: a. cross-curricula knowledge in say Maths skills through the songs, acts, etc., pertaining to numbers, days of the week, and seasons and months of the year; b. about nature, weather, and the seasons; c. history and geography; d. rite-de-passage; e. festivals when relating to the community; f. language arts skills when expressing themselves through L1 and L2 mediums, etc.
Project-Based Learning: Individually write down how your life experiences, ideas, and perspectives realized connect to everyday life.
